audit.why: 49.36% over 2255 games is genuinely even, and EVEN 5.5/10 with a 6/10 carry threat reflects that. This is the only matchup in my slice where the difficulty block was already right, and the sample is by far the largest.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart calls levels 1 through 4-5 'Skill' in both layers, and hands level 6 to Locke. The packet chart and every why say Graves / Graves / Graves / Graves / Skill / Locke / Skill. spikes[] also has only 3 entries where 4 are expected.
audit.why: whys[0] literally reads 'Level 1 is Graves', whys[2] 'Level 3 is Graves', whys[4] 'Level 6 evens things out'. All five contradicted rows sit directly above the sentence that contradicts them, and the early block calls levels 1-5 a period where 'you are simply the bigger bully'.
audit.corrected: Both charts flipped as one atomic group, and the missing fourth spike created with 'before': null — his R gaining power per champion sealed is the late-game scaling the page never named.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two Graves ability names on this page are fabricated. 'Buckshot' appears three times — Graves has no ability called Buckshot; his Q is End of the Line and the four-pellet spread is his passive, New Destiny. And Smoke Screen is called a blind that 'switches off the auto pattern his passive chip depends on' — it reduces sight range and slows on impact; nothing in it stops an attack landing.
audit.why: The blind claim is load-bearing here in a way it is not elsewhere: Locke's passive is on-hit magic damage on his attacks, so the page is specifically promising that W turns off his main damage source. It does not. A player holding W as a defensive answer to his auto pattern will take the full trade.
audit.corrected: Buckshot replaced with the real point-blank pellet spread and End of the Line; the blind replaced with Smoke Screen's impact slow, which is genuinely the tool that pins him for a volley.

audit.whatIsWrong: His Q is called 'Ritual Nails' in nine places. The only name Riot's text for that slot actually contains is Soul Nails.
audit.why: It is the focus ability of the whole page — the loading screen, the focus text and the cooldown block all key off it — so the one name a player reads most often is the one that is wrong.
audit.corrected: Corrected in whys and spikes where the string was writable in my layer. The focus.text and loading strings carry the same error and are listed in notes; I did not rewrite the focus block because it is repeated verbatim in six places and a partial fix would leave the page inconsistent.
sources: enemyKit Q text ('Locke readies a set of Soul Nails to throw')

audit.whatIsWrong: His W is never mentioned. It damages HIM during the effect and only heals a portion of that back AT THE END of the duration.
audit.why: That is a real kill window and the page has none: while W is running he has voluntarily lowered his own health and has not been refunded yet. Kill him inside it and the refund never happens. It is 18 seconds at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Written into the mid block as the concrete all-in cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' and the page repeatedly says 'ten seconds' without ever tying it to a spell.
audit.why: His E is a flat 10 seconds at every rank and 425 range — the same range as Quickdraw. That is the cleanest sequencing rule in the matchup.
audit.corrected: The flat 10s and the 425/425 range parity written into phases[1], phases[2] and whys[1].

edits.before: Levels 1-5 you are simply the bigger bully: double-shell autos and Buckshot out-trade his chip, Smoke Screen blinds his answer mid-pattern, and Quickdraw armor wins the level-3 duel outright. Force a trade every wave and convert into plates — this lead is the whole matchup, because his level 6 rewrites the rules on you.
edits.after: Levels 1-5 you are simply the bigger bully: two chambered shells at point-blank out-trade his nail chip, Smoke Screen's impact slow pins him for the volley, and dashing AT him for two True Grit stacks wins the level-3 duel outright. Force a trade every wave and convert it into plates — this lead is the whole matchup, because his level 6 rewrites the rules on you.

edits.before: From his 6 through first item, respect the flip: Purgatory executes a squishy Graves under threshold, and his burst spike makes one caught rotation lethal. Trade from grass angles at full HP only, keep Quickdraw charged as an exit rather than a poke tool, and spend your early gold lead on the map — you no longer need to beat him in lane.
edits.after: From his 6 through first item, respect the flip: his R executes a squishy Graves under threshold, and one caught rotation is lethal. One window stays yours — his W damages him to buy the attack-speed burst and only refunds a portion at the END of the duration, so a Collateral Damage inside that window kills through the heal that never arrives. Otherwise trade from grass at full HP, keep Quickdraw as the exit, and spend your gold lead on the map.

edits.before: Two-plus items it is an honest skill fight: your item damage trades evenly against his reliable execute, so discipline decides it. Fight around Smoke Screen and your dash resets, never show below half HP, and use superior waveclear to control picks. Buckshot bursts into a well-placed blind win the exact exchanges he wants to start.
edits.after: Two-plus items it is an honest skill fight: your item damage trades evenly against his reliable execute, so discipline decides it. Fight around Smoke Screen and your dash resets, never show below half HP, and use superior waveclear to control picks. End of the Line into a smoke slow wins the exact exchanges he wants to start.

notes: Locke's kit file carries no ability names for any slot — the only proper noun anywhere in Riot's text is 'Soul Nails' in the Q description. The page calls that ability 'Ritual Nails' in nine places, including focus.text, loading, breakdown.cooldowns and four report entries. I corrected it where the string was mine to change and left the focus/loading/report block alone rather than half-fix a name that is repeated verbatim; that block still needs a pass. The names 'Purgatory' (R) and 'Ashen Pursuit' (E) cannot be checked against anything in the data — I neither used nor removed them, and they are listed as unverified. Same for the page's claim that he is a '125-range mana champ': the kit gives no attack range, and his Q is 950 and his E 425, so nothing in the data supports or refutes 125. Last item: the derived flag on his R includes 'grounding: shuts off enemy dashes', which would disable Quickdraw and would be the single most important interaction on the page — but Riot's description says only that it binds, damages and potentially executes. I did not write it in.
